title: Christ the mediator of both natures
english: Epiphanius of Cyprus, from the discourse on faith.

And in order that Epiphanius might show that Christ is “mediator of God and human beings” (1 Timothy 2:5), possessing both realities—flesh from human beings and invisible essence from the Father—Christ speaks as God the divine things that are fitting for God, and as man the same one speaks the human things that are fitting for a human. In both he holds authority naturally and substantially, without confusion and without division, in both ways divinely and humanly.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
Single-paragraph fragment witness (Khazarzar one-page PDF); open-only, no rem sections.
orientation: The excerptor reports what Epiphanius of Cyprus showed in his discourse on faith, namely that Christ is mediator of God and human beings because he possesses both flesh from humanity and invisible essence from the Father.
